html:
The Chinchorro were fishing people of the Pacific coast of northern Chile and southern Peru, from about 7000 to 1500 BCE. They made the oldest known artificial mummies in the world. The map shows them in 2000 BCE.

They lived along one of the driest coasts on earth, at the edge of the Atacama Desert, where small rivers meet a cold sea rich in fish. They were settled but did not farm, living on fish, shellfish, sea lions and seabirds, with hooks and harpoons.

From about 5000 BCE, some two thousand years before Egypt, they began to mummify their dead. They took the body apart, removed organs and flesh, rebuilt it with sticks, reeds and clay, and covered it with a painted mask and wig. They gave this treatment to everyone, including babies and unborn children, not only to rulers.

The first mummies were described by Max Uhle in 1917. The sites around Arica were listed by UNESCO in 2021, and the mummies are now threatened by rising humidity.
